comment.name: Millard J Melnyk
comment.body:
The problem with all thinking like this is the fact that it surreptitiously and insidiously pretends, without cause or grounds, that the fictitious entities manipulated in the imaginary world of political and legal entities -- all of them absolutely, incorrigibly, definitionally, and ontologically abstract and disconnected from the real world -- are in fact connected to the real world. 

Well, no they're not. But the longer you tell elaborate stories based on the presumption that they are, the more they will appear to be so to those who keep listening to your yarns.

comment.name: Millard J Melnyk
comment.body:
What makes this so difficult for people to understand?

If it's "no longer" a conspiracy theory, then it NEVER WAS a conspiracy theory, period.

That is, except to the *actual* conspiracy theorists -- people who lack the the ability to see the difference between truth and bullshit unless a talking head on their screen tells them what to think. 

Those are the people who call ideas "conspiracy theories" for no other reason than that facts exist which don't fit with their preconceived beliefs.

Which gives you a pretty clear read on the nature and quality of their beliefs.
